newsitem.title: CONGO: U.S., French, Belgian troops mass near Zaire.
newsitem.headline: U.S., French, Belgian troops mass near Zaire.

text.p: American, French and Belgian troops massed in Congo's capital on Tuesday, ready to evacuate thousands of Westerners from neighbouring Zaire if the crisis there degenerates, diplomatic sources said.
They said about one thousand soldiers were already in Brazzaville with more expected.

The city's Maya-Maya airport was virtually a military base as heavy transport planes roared in from Europe carrying men, arms and equipment. Tents for the soldiers and their weaponry sprouted like mushrooms inside the airport.

The three Western allies say the force's mission is entirely humanitarian. The troops will only cross the mighty Zaire river into Kinshasa, Zaire's capital, to evacuate foreigners if necessary, Belgium's ambassador to Congo, Eric Foke, told reporters on Tuesday.
Rebels have captured about one quarter of Zaire in the past five months, routing President Mobutu Sese Seko's ragged army.
But they are still about 1,000 km (625 miles) from Kinshasa which is tense but calm and with no reports of attacks on foreigners.
The size of the foreign force and its rapid deployment in the past 48 hours have led to rumours in both Kinshasa and Brazzaville that its real purpose is to save Mobutu's 32-year regime.
"Congo has chosen to help out Mobutu's regime at the request of France," one of Brazzaville's pro-opposition newspapers said.
France has remained loyal to Mobutu, its long-time ally, but has made clear throughout Laurent Kabila's five-month-old rebellion it will not intervene militarily to save his regime.

Regional analysts noted that the presence of several hundred American troops in Brazzaville also weakened the local conspiracy theory. Although Washington was Mobutu's main sponsor when he took power in 1965, it has withdrawn all support and is now seen as closer to the rebel cause.

The French and Belgian armies have several times intervened in Zaire during periodic crises during the Mobutu era. They evacuated foreigners during massive looting sprees by impoverished troops and civilians in 1993 and 1991.
But if they cross the river into Kinshasa, U.S. troops will be involved in a major evacuation operation from Zaire for the first time.
